papers.title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(\delta t)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $\kappa(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

papers.title: Passive ladder-network representation of the radiation impedance of a spherical cap on a rigid sphere
papers.abstract: A loudspeaker in a closed box is modeled as a rigid sphere with an axially moving cap. For an axisymmetric cone-velocity profile, its radiation impedance is written as a network. Each spherical-harmonic mode has an impedance rational in frequency, realized exactly as a finite passive ladder of masses and compliances terminated in a resistance. Ideal transformers set by Legendre coefficients couple these ladders; truncated modes reduce to a residual mass. Despite the different geometry, the impedance resembles that of a baffled piston but, at equal volume velocity, has half its low-frequency resistance and about three quarters of its radiation mass.

papers.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
papers.abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.

papers.title: Energy Dissipation Modulates Sensitivity to Corner Advantage in Weighted Dice
papers.abstract: Weighted dice have pedagogical value and a range of broader implications. The physics of such dice provides an entry point for understanding state probabilities, center-of-mass calculations, and inertia tensors. Related considerations arise in the physics of grains, seed dispersal, erosion, and materials science, all of which involve components that can be compared with the stochastic tumbling and settling of dice. Previous empirical results are consistent with a Boltzmann-like distribution. We reproduce this result at scale using 23 classes of corner-loaded dice and more than 500,000 physical dice rolls collected with an automated rolling and imaging system. Briefly, landing probability increases exponentially with corner advantage (lower center-of-mass). We test the additional hypothesis that landing statistics depend on the combined effects of corner advantage, inertia tensor, and energy dissipation. Corner advantage defines the direction of the gravitational preference, but the rate of energy dissipation determines how strongly that preference is expressed in the final landing distribution. Simulations suggest that the inertia tensor and its orientation affect roll statistics; indeed, we find a small but statistically detectable departure from uniform landing probabilities under our experimental conditions. Our approach has pedagogical value as an entry-level engineering and data science project. The dice are 3D-printed and automatically rolled at scale using affordable parts and open-source tools. Results are compared to rigid-body simulations and a six-state model of energy dissipation.

papers.title: The Feynman Dyson argument extended to the inhomogeneous Maxwell equations
papers.abstract: The Feynman-Dyson argument gives the homogeneous Maxwell equations but does not identify the sources in the other two equations with the charge and current carried by matter. Taking the homogeneous equations as given, we derive Gauss's law and the Ampere-Maxwell law for the sources entering the Lorentz force and the power delivered to matter. We assume, in particular, that the field densities and fluxes are at most quadratic in the fields and covariant under proper rotations. We require the same expressions for the sources to satisfy local energy and momentum conservation for every field that obeys the homogeneous equations, and to be continuous in spacetime along every smooth such field. The charge and current densities are then unique up to the values of $\varepsilon_0$ and $\mu_0$. We also discuss how these assumptions might be relaxed.

papers.title: Mapping the limits of equilibrium in sheared granular liquid crystals
papers.abstract: While elongated particles in viscous fluids follow Jeffery orbits, their dynamics in dense granular flows remain unresolved. We demonstrate that sheared, low friction granular rods do not follow these orbits, but instead reach a quasi-equilibrium state quantitatively described by classical liquid crystal theory, with collisions providing effective thermal noise. This quasi-equilibrium analogy breaks down at two limits: low aspect ratios, where the theory incorrectly predicts isotropy, and high inter-particle friction, which drives a transition from steric screening to frictional gearing. We map this far-from-equilibrium breakdown using a phenomenological effective Ericksen number, establishing the limits of thermal thermodynamic analogies in driven athermal matter.

papers.title: Point Charges in Classical Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: LaTeX transcription (2025) of a 1989 honours thesis (University of Adelaide) on point charges in classical electrodynamics and the Lorentz-Dirac radiation-reaction equation. The thesis reviews the retarded field of an arbitrarily moving charge, energy-momentum conservation, and derives the Lorentz-Dirac equation via momentum balance. It discusses self-interaction and mass renormalization, and presents world-line self-field definitions including retarded averaging and an analytic continuation approach. Appendices include Mathematica listings used to obtain near-world-line expansions of the field and related quantities.

papers.title: Contact mechanics and friction of soft materials: an apparatus combining multi-axes dynamical actuation/measurement and in situ/in operando visualisation
papers.abstract: The mechanics and friction of contact interfaces involving soft materials like gel, rubber or human skin are of both fundamental and applied interest. Recent insights have been made into this field thanks to in situ observations of the contact interface. However, current soft-material--oriented tribometers enable only few degrees of freedom for the actuation of the contact, far from covering the richness of the loading conditions relevant to real tribological contacts. Here, we introduce an instrument dedicated to the study of the contact mechanics and friction of soft materials which, in addition to in situ / in operando optical monitoring of the interface, enables simultaneous actuation along five degrees of freedom: three translations and two rotations. While all three translations feature large velocity/large stroke motion, the one responsible for normal contact loading can also apply high frequency/small amplitude vibrations. The contact's dynamical response is monitored using both a 6-axes force/torque sensor and a 6-axes displacement/rotation sensor. We first describe the structure of the instrument, its implementation, alignment, calibration and resolutions. We then illustrate its capabilities through a series of experiments on elastomer contacts. Our instrument will be useful to investigate the mechanics of a wide range of soft interfaces submitted to rich, tribology-relevant kinematic or dynamic stimuli.
